names: a guide whose release states its period where the reader did not look is no longer filed under the next-fy default: a list header written straight after the previous list's last bullet heads its own list, a list item's ';'-ended tail is never a header, a header that says what its outlook rests on ('Based on our first half 2026 results …') is read at the clause its forward verb opens, a guide joined by 'and' to its partner's range takes the partner's period, and 'full year' in the guide's own clause is FY; and a one-off item carries the period its release places it in ('Q2 2026', '2025', 'six months ended June 30, 2026'), stated in the synthesis digest and the gap-driver line, with the full-year impairment never a quarter's, a year-to-date span's or one whose period was not read (audit RE2-D20, RE2-D17, RE2-D6's residual: an amount a component phrase ('including an SRE impact of') attaches to the figure before it is not that figure's lead, RE2-D10's other half: a 10-Q read through its notes with no doubt statement is a CHECKED-ABSENT going-concern read, not None; and, on #1027's pre-draw review: a period inside a header's 'Based on …' clause is the outlook's basis, never the guided period, so Verra Mobility's Q3 2025 full-year guides no longer read Q4; a CHECKED-ABSENT going-concern read needs the notes' heading followed by notes with body text, never a sentence naming the notes or a contents entry (Lilly's 'Consolidated Condensed' order and McKesson's 'Financial Notes' read as headings); an item whose own sentence names no period, after a sentence comparing year-to-date figures, is unread, not the quarter's; and the release's own year in a first-, second- or third-quarter release is unread, not its full year)
